What the model is. A multimodal late-interaction (multi-vector) retriever: one
L2-normalized 128-dim vector per kept token, retrieval score = fp32 MaxSim,
client-side. The checkpoint is a native sentence-transformers export -- no
custom Python code anywhere (the card says so; the repo has no auto_map, no
modeling file, and the modules.json lists only native ST classes). The
pipeline: the Qwen3.5 backbone (bidirectional; text_config.is_causal false)
-> 1_Dense Linear(1024 -> 128, no bias) -> 2_MultiVectorMask (documents drop
the 32 ASCII punctuation token positions; queries keep everything) ->
3_Normalize (L2). Text prompts are NOT chat-formatted on the wire: the
sentence-transformers prompts are "[Q] " and "[D] "
(config_sentence_transformers.json), both ADDED special tokens of this
tokenizer (ids 248077/248078), and the render "[Q] " + text /
"[D] " + text tokenizes to [248077|248078] + body under the engine-side
parse -- measured, and identical to the reference's (sentence-transformers
uses no split_special_tokens anywhere, unlike pplx-embed-v2-context-9b's
remote code; that divergence is why that recipe rides token_ids and this one
rides text).

The served vs reference rendering contract (stage 1):
- query shape: "[Q] " + query; every query token keeps its vector (the
  skiplist applies to documents only, skiplist_tasks ["document"]).
- document shape: "[D] " + document; every token NOT in the 32 punctuation
  ids keeps its vector. The prefix token (248078) is an added special token,
  not punctuation, so it keeps its vector on both sides -- unlike topk, where
  the prompt's own colon was dropped. The mask is the checkpoint's own
  MultiVectorMask; the recipe DECLARES it (client.document_skip_token_ids,
  resolved from skiplist_words with this tokenizer exactly as
  sentence-transformers' resolve_with_tokenizer does) and the client drops
  the vectors at the ids it sent, cross-checking the counts.
- No content normalisation: sentence-transformers prepends the prompt
  verbatim (prepend_prompt_to_texts), so the declared normalize is [] and
  every text ships as-is. The empty-document corner that forced topk's
  omit_zero does not exist here: the reference's empty document renders the
  bare "[D] " prompt -- exactly one kept token (the prefix id, no skiplist
  word) -- and empty_doc: send renders the same frame around empty content.
  The empty-document rows gate exactly, and the wave's pairs may sample them.

pinned revision and vLLM resolves it through AutoProcessor for the
pooling-chat (media) path; a missing template there is a loud per-request
error, never a silent fallback. The template is a pass-through render (system
text first, then vision markers, then text parts; no im-start/im-end
wrappers), which is why the reference's chat-templated TEXT renders are
byte-identical to the plain prompts the /pooling route reads (the route
applies no template -- poolings/protocol.py at the tag). Shipping a copy
would add a second source of truth for a file the engine already pins through
the revision. The harness's stage-1 template check cannot render a
messages-based template (it renders query/document variables), so the
recipe's test pins the image wrapper structure directly instead.

new PplxLateMultiVectorModel subclasses the native ColQwen3_5Model and (a)
registers the checkpoint's architecture name "Qwen3_5Model" with vLLM's
registry, (b) inherits the stock mapper that maps this checkpoint's top-level
"language_model.*" onto the class's "language_model.model.*" (visual.*
matches as-is; the absent lm_head is the tied alias of embed_tokens and
loads as its skipped alias), and (c) loads the Dense head itself: the

Budget: max_tokens 4096 is the document cap and query_max_tokens 1024 the
query cap -- each the shape's whole rendered prompt as the engine sees it, in
the tokenizer's tokens, right truncation (sentence-transformers passes
truncation="longest_first" with the per-task max_length on every text
encode). on_overflow: cut: the content span only, the fixed head reserved,
the template re-attached (the product's fit, one budget per shape). The
card's own cut (that truncation) right-cuts the rendered prompt's ids;
reference.py renders exactly that cut, located by character offsets. Both
cuts keep the fixed head and the same text on every input measured (English,
punctuation-heavy, CJK, emoji and repeated-letter content), but the card cuts
ids, not text: when its last kept id lands inside a character spanning
several byte-level tokens (an emoji), the card's model reads that character's
leading bytes, which no text carries -- one more id than the client sends.
Hence over_cap_cut_differs (the anchor kept, the kept content differing by
that id; a stage-2 difference, the render texts are equal). max_model_len
4352 reserves the 4096-token document budget + 256 headroom; image documents
cost at most 1 + 2 + 1,758 = 1,761 tokens (the "[D] " prompt token, the
vision start/end markers, the shipped pixel budget) -- under the text cap,
so one max_model_len covers both shapes.
